subject: Biotechnology
title: The Asilomar Conference
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Asilomar Conference.

hook.text: In 1975 scientists voluntarily paused their own research — fearing recombinant DNA could create unstoppable pathogens.

buildup.text: Berg, Boyer, and Cohen pioneered gene splicing — but what if engineered bacteria escaped the lab and spread new genes?

discovery.text: 140 scientists met at Asilomar to set safety guidelines — containment levels matched to risk, from minimal to maximum.

twist.text: Critics argued scientists regulated themselves to prevent harsher government laws — self-governance had strategic motives.

climax.text: Asilomar's framework shaped the NIH Guidelines for recombinant DNA — still the foundation of lab biosafety worldwide.

punchline.text: Scientists who paused to ask if they should — Asilomar defined responsible biotech.

quiz.question: What was the outcome of the 1975 Asilomar Conference?
options: All recombinant DNA research was permanently banned
Scientists established safety guidelines matching containment levels to biological risk
The government took full control of all genetic engineering research
